profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at athenaHealth
profile.summary:
Certified Scrum Master (scrumalliance.org)

Experienced Senior Software Engineer with a demonstrated history of working in the data storage and management industry. Multiple years experience in firmware development for storage hardware (DRAM and SSD caching) as well as software development for "middleware" applications (deduplication, data clone and snapshots, cloud replication). Holds a Master's degree in Computer Science from Boston University, and a Bachelor's degree in Mathematics/Computer Science from University of Massachusetts.

positions.title: Principal Software Engineer
positions.description:
Actifio virtualizes the data that’s the lifeblood of businesses in more than 30 countries around the world. Its Virtual Data Pipeline™ technology enables businesses to protect, access, and move their data faster, more efficiently, and more simply by decoupling data from physical storage, much the same way a hypervisor decouples compute from physical servers. For enterprise-class backup modernization, self-serve instant data access, or service provider business transformation, Actifio is the first and only choice for radically simple copy data virtualization. For more visit Actifio.com, or follow us on Twitter @Actifio.

Member of the Engineering team, originally responsible for development of the block-level deduplication component, now focused on development of software to enable using cloud services as a block-level backend for our copy data virtualization platform.

positions.title: Principal Software Engineer
positions.description:
USD CLARiiON Array Software Engineering
Internal driver software development for CLARiiON CX and VNX series storage array product line. Worked to maintain and develop new features for WDM filter drivers on custom hardware running Windows O/S (XPe, Server 2K3, 2K8). Primary development work done in C/C++; test scripting / automation in    Perl. Extensive work done using both procedural and object oriented programming.
Bugfix & code optimization for onboard DRAM cache driver. Implemented    new features that allow for more robust fault tolerance & increase    availability through maintenance periods or reboots/failures of Storage Processors (SP) by allowing for DMA copy of cache image from one SP to  the other, and allow for rebuilding cache image from data that is persisted     in DRAM cache after system reboot. Participated in porting driver for use     on new 64 bit O/S. Worked on low-level enhancements to increase performance on multi-core Intel processor architectures.
Worked on enhancements to proprietary EMC basic object library that is   used across all internally developed drivers.
Designed and implemented new software library to allow clients to more efficiently move blocks of data internally between storage units. Assisted various groups within EMC with integrating this feature into their layered drivers.
Designed and implemented new cache driver that utilizes Solid State Disks (SSDs) to store blocks of data that are found to be accessed frequently.     The "flash cache" driver allowed for up to 2TB of data to be remapped from slower speed Hard Disk Drives (HDDs) throughout the system (up to 960 physical disks) to high speed SSDs.

patents.title: Method, data storage system and computer program product for managing copy on first write data for snapshot purposes
patents.description: A data storage system, method and computer program product for managing copy on first write data for snapshot purposes are disclosed. In one embodiment, a determination is made whether new data is a first update of original data in a first section of a data storage device in response to receiving a write instruction to write the new data. The new data is provided to a first location of a cache memory and the original data to a second location of the cache memory. Providing the new data to the first location in the cache memory is not dependent on whether the original data has been copied from the data storage device. Further, the original data can be provided to the second location of the cache memory after new data is provided to first location of the cache memory. Completion of the write instruction is confirmed in response to providing the new data to the first location of the cache memory.
